title: Giants send Luis Matos to Brewers for cash, acquire Dylan Smith from Tigers
content:
SAN DIEGO — Outfielder Luis Matos doesn’t post thunderous exit velocities. He doesn’t rank high on the sprint speed leaderboard. Yet, immersed in an industry obsessed with physical tools, Matos found himself on the back end of Baseball America’s top-100 prospects list four years ago.

He was so polished at the plate. He struck out so seldomly. And he was competing against older players as a 19-year-old at Low-A San Jose. Matos was ranked so highly, and the San Francisco Giants were so excited about his potential because he displayed so much aptitude for playing the game. And he would only get stronger as he continued to mature physically.

Four years later, as cruel as it might be to acknowledge, Matos aged out. It seems a harsh verdict for someone who celebrated his 24th birthday in January, but the Giants ran out of time. Matos hadn’t developed the physicality that would allow his hitting ability to translate into sufficiently hard contact against major league pitching. And he was out of minor league options. Jerar Encarnacion offered more power and Jared Oliva offered more speed and defense. So the Giants designated Matos for assignment when he didn’t crack their Opening Day roster.

It seems a shame to lose a top-100 prospect to a waiver claim, as the Giants did with catcher Joey Bart a few years ago. Matos didn’t stand much of a chance of sneaking through waivers, which would have allowed the Giants to outright him to Triple-A. So it wasn’t a shock when the Giants traded Matos to a club that wanted to jump the waiver priority line. They dealt him to the Milwaukee Brewers for cash considerations.

The Brewers used a lineup filled with high-contact, low-strikeout hitters to post the best record in the National League last season. Perhaps they’ll be able to turn Matos’ reliable contact rate into something that can fill up box scores in the big leagues.

Matos was a .291 hitter over six minor league seasons, and in parts of three major league seasons, he hit .231/.281/.369 with 15 home runs in 593 plate appearances. He had a memorable run in May 2024 when he won NL Player of the Week honors while wedging himself into the franchise record book. When Matos drove in 11 runs over a two-game span, he matched the modern franchise record set by Hall of Famer Bill Terry in 1932 and matched by Jack Clark in 1982. It was the most RBIs by a big leaguer 22 years or younger in consecutive games since Cincinnati Reds Hall of Famer Johnny Bench in 1970.

The Matos trade was one of three roster tweaks the Giants made before Monday’s series opener against the San Diego Padres, although it won’t result in any changes to the active group that is reporting to Petco Park.

The team also acquired right-handed reliever Dylan Smith from the Detroit Tigers for cash. They designated infielder and 2025 Opening Day second baseman Tyler Fitzgerald for assignment to create a 40-man roster spot for Smith.

Smith, 25, posted a 1.38 ERA in 13 innings for the Tigers last season and struck out 57 over 39 2/3 innings across four minor league levels; he’d been designated for assignment before Opening Day when Detroit needed his 40-man spot for another player.
